newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ANGRY BASTIA FANS PELT PITCH AFTER MORAVCIK INJURED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY BASTIA FANS PELT PITCH AFTER MORAVCIK INJURED.

text.p: Angry Bastia fans hurled missiles on to the pitch after an unpunished tackle by Monaco's Emmanuel Petit left Slovakian striker Lubomir Moravcik with a fractured ankle in a goalless draw in their French first division match on Saturday.
The referee was hit by a missile but play was resumed after a delay of several minutes.

Monaco and Bastia had begun the day in joint second place but the draw enabled champions Auxerre to leapfrog over them with a 1-0 home win over Lens through a 76th minute penalty by midfielder Antoine Sibierski.
None of it made any impact on leaders Paris Saint-Germain who moved seven points clear with Brazilian midfielder Leonardo scoring his seventh goal of the season in their 1-0 home win over Lens.

Jean-Pierre Papin's Bordeaux crashed to their second successive home defeat, beaten 1-0 by bottom club Nancy who registered their first win of the season through a seventh-minute goal by Northern Ireland international Phil Gray.
Bordeaux were reduced to 10 men shortly before the end when Kaba Diawara was sent off for dissent after the referee refused the home side a penalty.
